top.title: Russell Brand jailed for 10 years for rape, assault
top.description: British comedian and TV star Russell Brand was Monday jailed for more than 10 years for a string of sex offences including rape, as the judge told him he had been a “sexual predator” whose fame had protected him. Brand, 51, showed no emotion as judge Joel Bennathan said he had acted with “staggering arrogance” and shown “contempt” for his victims, who had suffered significant and lasting harm. “About 20 years ago Russell Brand, you were becoming famous, you were clever, and in many people’s eyes you were funny and charismatic. You had also become a sexual predator,” he said. The judge said Brand’s status protected him until he was exposed in 2023 by journalists from the Sunday Times, The Times and the Channel 4 Dispatches programme, leading to women coming forward to make complaints to police. Bennathan paid tribute to the “determination and bravery” of the women, adding Brand had repeatedly acted “how you liked and when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live”. Brand’s wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he has three children, slumped in her seat in the public gallery of London’s Southwark Crown Court as the total sentence of 10 years and six months was announced. Brand told his wife, who has supported him in court throughout the case, “we’ll be OK”, before being led down to the cells. The disgraced star was convicted by a jury last week of one rape and three sexual assaults committed against four women between 2004 and 2009. Brand, who has reinvented himself as an online Christian guru, held a string of prayer beads and made the sign of the cross before one of his victims personally read out her impact statement from behind a screen. She said she had been left “traumatised” by the assault in a London bar in 2004. “For many years as his star was rising it was impossible to escape seeing him all over the media, being celebrated for his disgusting behaviour against women like it was all a joke,” she told the court. ‘Celebrated’ A second woman, a 21-year-old fan he raped in 2009 after they met at one of his shows, told the court she had felt she simply would “not be believed” if she reported him. “His fame, wealth and influence created a power imbalance which made me feel powerless,” she said. The hearing came as Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to be “relentless in making whatever improvements we can” to provide more support for victims. Brand was cleared of two other alleged rapes and one count of attempted indecent assault. But he is facing further investigations after London police revealed rape allegations by two more women. From Channel 4 to MTV and an eponymous primetime show on BBC Radio 2, the wild-haired comedian’s obsession with sex and his no-holds barred delivery contributed to his notoriety. top.title: Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission
top.description: null Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier. The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable. The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase. Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX 's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher , Google's planned AI constellation). The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short. The goal was to "demonstrate technologies necessary for future debris-removal missions as well as for future applications in the servicing and inspection of active spacecraft," according to NASA's SSPICY site . "This advances NASA's in-space manufacturing and assembly (ISAM) goals to ensure a sustainable space operating environment and builds towards a future where objects can be assembled, repaired and maintained in space, significantly expanding possibilities for science and human exploration," the agency added. Starfish Space was a natural partner. The Seattle company plans to become a big player in the nascent field of satellite servicing , using its line of Otter craft to repair, refuel or deorbit other satellites for a variety of customers. Illustration of a Starfish Space Otter satellite rendesvousing with another spacecraft in Earth orbit. (Image credit: Starfish Space) SSPICY marked Otter's spaceflight debut. The mission plan called for the 739-pound (335-kilogram) Otter 24C spacecraft to approach and inspect "up to four inoperable space objects of U.S. origin" over the course of a two-year mission, performing detailed visual inspections. But Otter 24C never got the chance to perform any of these orbital rendezvous. "While working through commissioning steps, Starfish eventually stopped receiving data from Otter 24C," the company said in a Nov. 3 X post . "An investigation into the loss of communications has determined that fault protection on the satellite bus provided by [California company] Astro Digital had an error that turned off the radio and prevented re-establishing communications," Starfish added. "Starfish, NASA, and Astro Digital have concluded that Otter 24C is not recoverable." The company further said that it's implementing fixes to reduce the chances that the problem will crop up in the future. And it stressed that Otter 24C's death will not be in vain. "The work completed through Otter 24C will directly contribute to the success of future Otter missions, as Starfish continues developing the technologies and operations required to make satellite servicing a routine capability in orbit," Starfish said. Braden Fiske could become the trade asset that makes a potential deal possible, particularly if the Jacksonville Jaguars are willing to discuss Brian Thomas Jr. A Fiske-for-Thomas swap could make sense for both organizations. Fiske could provide the Jaguars with a young, disruptive defensive lineman who still has plenty of upside and multiple years of team control. James Gladstone, the Jaguars GM, was a big proponent of the Braden Fiske pick in 2024. Could he want to reunite with the 2nd rounder with shipping away Brian Thomas Jr to the Rams? top.title: Falcons say goodbye to former Bengals DB Jessie Bates III
top.description: Atlanta Falcons defensive back Jessie Bates III was traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars one day after the team's NFL Week 9 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals at Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. The Falcons thanked Bates with a tweet , "for everything on and off the field." The Bengals' second-round pick in the 2018 NFL Draft faced his former team for the first time since leaving Cincinnati for Atlanta after the 2022 season. Bates led the Falcons with 14 tackles against the Bengals, including 11 solo tackles. Bengals head coach Zac Taylor shared praise of Bates earlier in the week. "I feel like I've just seen him a lot on TV, on tape, and I think we all love Jessie," Taylor told reporters Nov. 2 . "Everybody feels the same way about Jessie here. And (I've) always been pulling for him and really happy to see him be successful, a Pro Bowler (in 2023), like he's earned all that and (is a) really easy guy to root for." Taylor coached Bates for four seasons. Bates played in 79 games over five seasons with the Bengals. He has played in 59 games over four seasons in Atlanta. Bates entered the game with one interception through eight games this season. He's returned an interception for a touchdown in each of the past three seasons. top.title: Is there an alternative to DLS? Exploring various methods to calculate scores in rain-affected matches
top.description: Is there an alternative to DLS? Exploring various methods to calculate scores in rain-affected matches originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: DLS calculates targets using resources, meaning overs remaining and wickets in hand together. The VJD method is the only serious modern rival, and it is used in Indian domestic cricket. Earlier systems failed because they ignored wickets, most notoriously at the 1992 World Cup. What is the DLS method? The Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method is the system cricket uses to reset a target when rain or any other interruption shortens a limited-overs match. It was devised by two English statisticians, Frank Duckworth and Tony Lewis, introduced in 1997 and adopted by the ICC two years later. Its central idea is that a batting side has two resources at any moment, overs remaining and wickets in hand, and that both have to be counted. A team 120 for 0 after 25 overs is in a far stronger position than one 120 for 9 after the same 25, and any fair method has to say so. DLS assigns every combination of overs and wickets a percentage of total resources, then adjusts the target in proportion to how much each side actually had. The method was renamed in November 2014, when Australian statistician Steven Stern took over as custodian and revised the model to reflect higher modern scoring rates, particularly in T20. It exists in two forms. The Standard Edition works from a printed table and can be applied with a calculator, which is what club and lower-level cricket use. The Professional Edition runs on software and is the version used in international cricket. MORE: What is the DLS method? Duckworth–Lewis rules explained for ODIs and T20Is What are the alternatives to the DLS method? Several systems have been used or proposed; some of them are predecessors, one cricket-abandoned, and one a genuine modern rival. Average Run Rate The oldest approach, used from the early days of one-day cricket until 1991. Team 2's target was simply Team 1's run rate multiplied by the reduced number of overs, so the chasing side only had to match the rate. Its flaw was that it ignored wickets entirely. A side nine down with a healthy run rate was treated identically to one that had lost nothing, which meant the method systematically favoured the team batting second. Every over removed was an over they no longer had to survive. Australia pushed hardest for its replacement, with Allan Border among those criticising it publicly after a defeat where a West Indies target was cut in a way that lowered their required rate rather than raising it. nigeria.title: Russell Brand jailed for 10 years for rape, assault
nigeria.description: British comedian and TV star Russell Brand was Monday jailed for more than 10 years for a string of sex offences including rape, as the judge told him he had been a “sexual predator” whose fame had protected him. Brand, 51, showed no emotion as judge Joel Bennathan said he had acted with “staggering arrogance” and shown “contempt” for his victims, who had suffered significant and lasting harm. “About 20 years ago Russell Brand, you were becoming famous, you were clever, and in many people’s eyes you were funny and charismatic. You had also become a sexual predator,” he said. The judge said Brand’s status protected him until he was exposed in 2023 by journalists from the Sunday Times, The Times and the Channel 4 Dispatches programme, leading to women coming forward to make complaints to police. Bennathan paid tribute to the “determination and bravery” of the women, adding Brand had repeatedly acted “how you liked and when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live”. Brand’s wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he has three children, slumped in her seat in the public gallery of London’s Southwark Crown Court as the total sentence of 10 years and six months was announced. Brand told his wife, who has supported him in court throughout the case, “we’ll be OK”, before being led down to the cells. The disgraced star was convicted by a jury last week of one rape and three sexual assaults committed against four women between 2004 and 2009. Brand, who has reinvented himself as an online Christian guru, held a string of prayer beads and made the sign of the cross before one of his victims personally read out her impact statement from behind a screen. She said she had been left “traumatised” by the assault in a London bar in 2004. “For many years as his star was rising it was impossible to escape seeing him all over the media, being celebrated for his disgusting behaviour against women like it was all a joke,” she told the court. ‘Celebrated’ A second woman, a 21-year-old fan he raped in 2009 after they met at one of his shows, told the court she had felt she simply would “not be believed” if she reported him. “His fame, wealth and influence created a power imbalance which made me feel powerless,” she said. The hearing came as Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to be “relentless in making whatever improvements we can” to provide more support for victims. Brand was cleared of two other alleged rapes and one count of attempted indecent assault. But he is facing further investigations after London police revealed rape allegations by two more women. From Channel 4 to MTV and an eponymous primetime show on BBC Radio 2, the wild-haired comedian’s obsession with sex and his no-holds barred delivery contributed to his notoriety. nigeria.title: 2027: Stop following Tinubu to rallies, return to grassroots, Kalu tells APC leaders
nigeria.description: Senator Orji Uzor Kalu has urged leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to stop following President Bola Tinubu from one campaign rally to another and concentrate on grassroots mobilisation in their respective states, local government areas and wards ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kalu, who represents Abia North Senatorial District and serves as Coordinator of Parliamentary Mobilisation for the South-East, made the call in a statement titled, “The APC Presidential Campaign Council and the Need for a Leaner Campaign Train.” He argued that Tinubu should be accompanied by a smaller campaign team, while other party leaders should remain in their respective political bases to engage voters and strengthen the party’s grassroots structures. The senator’s position comes days after the APC Presidential Campaign Council issued guidelines restricting ministers, political appointees and campaign council members to rallies organised in their respective home states. The circular, signed by the Director-General of the council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, on November 3, was addressed to directors and heads of directorates. It directed political appointees and other campaign officials to attend only rallies in their home states as part of efforts to improve coordination and grassroots mobilisation. The council also adopted what it described as the pyramid concept of mobilisation, which prioritises engagement at polling unit, ward, local government and state levels. Under the arrangement, campaign officials and party leaders are expected to concentrate on building support at the grassroots rather than concentrating around the President during rallies. Kalu cited his political activities in Abia State as an example of the importance of grassroots mobilisation. He recalled leading more than 4,000 APC members in his Igbere Ward A, Bende Local Government Area, during the party’s presidential primary in May. He said the exercise demonstrated the importance of building political support from the ward level. At the exercise, the returning officer, Mr Ulu Onwuchekwa, announced that Tinubu scored 4,986 votes in the ward. Tinubu had also urged members of the campaign council to take responsibility for mobilisation across the country, saying he would concentrate on governance. The President made the appeal on October 14 during the inauguration of the Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja. The campaign was subsequently flagged off in Kaduna on October 24, with plans to take the campaign to all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. Tinubu is, however, expected to personally attend rallies in only 12 states. nigeria.title: Man Utd delay decision on Carrick’s future after dropping into relegation zone — report
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United are not in a hurry to sack head coach Michael Carrick despite their drop into the Premier League relegation zone following Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, according to Sky Sports . Sky Sports News reports that the club’s hierarchy plan to use the international break to assess the team’s poor start to the season and reconsider their options before making a decision on Carrick’s future. The former United midfielder is under increasing pressure after the club recorded just one win in 11 matches, conceded 30 goals in all competitions and endured what has been described as their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign. United’s 4-4 draw against Villa followed another comeback in their previous match, but the recent results have not been enough to ease concerns over their overall performances. Carrick and his players were given Monday off after the Villa encounter, with the head coach and his staff expected to return to the club’s Carrington training base on Tuesday. With several players away on international duty and no first-team training sessions scheduled in the coming days, the break is expected to give the club’s leadership time to conduct a broader review. According to Sky Sports, three major factors have contributed to the hierarchy’s decision not to rush a change in the dugout. First, United supporters have not called for Carrick to be dismissed, with the former midfielder still enjoying considerable affection from the fanbase because of his achievements as a player. Carrick won 11 major trophies during his playing career at Old Trafford, including the Champions League and five Premier League titles. Secondly, the club’s hierarchy believe the 45-year-old still has the support of the dressing room, despite the team’s poor form. The recent comebacks against Roma in the Champions League and Aston Villa in the Premier League are understood to have reinforced the belief that the players have not given up on their manager. Thirdly, United’s decision-makers are reportedly not convinced that replacing Carrick would automatically resolve the team’s problems, with the performances of the players also under scrutiny. The report adds that the club could consider available managerial options, including Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe, if they eventually decide to make a change. For now, however, United are expected to take their time before deciding whether Carrick remains the right man to lead the club out of their current crisis. nigeria.title: Joe Biden scales back book tour as cancer ‘slows me down’
nigeria.description: Former US president Joe Biden says he is scaling back plans to promote his upcoming memoir as he battles aggressive prostate cancer, acknowledging that the illness sometimes leaves him struggling. The 83-year-old Democrat, whose health was a major issue during his presidency, said Sunday that he would be unable to make as many public appearances as he had hoped ahead of the November 17 release of “Promise Me, America.” “Some days are better than others. It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down,” Biden wrote on X. “What that means is, unfortunately, I won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped. However, I’m hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves.” Biden announced in May 2025, four months after leaving the White House, that he had been diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer that had spread to his bones. He has since undergone radiation and hormone therapy, while his son Hunter said in August that the disease had spread further and was causing considerable pain. Biden struck an optimistic note about his treatment, saying his doctors “continue to be encouraged” by his response. His memoir chronicles his four years in the White House, including his handling of the Covid-19 pandemic, wars in Afghanistan and Ukraine, and his controversial decision to seek reelection in 2024 before withdrawing. In an excerpt published Monday by The Atlantic, Biden delivered a blistering attack on his successor Donald Trump over the 2021 assault on the US Capitol by supporters seeking to overturn Trump’s election defeat. “What Trump did on January 6, 2021, should never be forgotten. It should follow him to his grave,” Biden wrote. He also recalled an unexpectedly friendly Oval Office meeting with Trump following the Republican’s 2024 election victory, during which his successor suggested they might have been friends outside politics. Biden abandoned his reelection campaign in July 2024 after a disastrous debate against Trump intensified concerns about his age and fitness for office. His vice president, Kamala Harris, subsequently lost the election, returning Trump to the White House. Biden said his book would explain the decisions he made in office and reflect his faith in American democracy. nigeria.title: Why getting most votes is not enough to become Nigeria’s president
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – No candidate can become Nigeria’s president simply by polling the highest number of votes. The 1999 Constitution also demands that the winner shows support across the federation. Read Also: * What is 25% requirement in Nigeria’s presidential election? * 2027: What happens when Nigerian election results are disputed? Also, there is no fixed number of votes that guarantees victory in presidential. Neither 10 million nor 15 million votes means anything on its own. Two conditions are set out in Section 134(2) of the Constitution. A candidate must first have “the highest number of votes cast at the election.” The second condition is the spread. The candidate must have “not less than one-quarter of the votes cast at the election in each of at least two-thirds of all the states in Nigeria and the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja.” Nigeria has 36 states, and two-thirds of 36 is 24. The arithmetic is less settled once the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, is counted as a 37th unit, because two-thirds of 37 is about 24.7. Lawyer Femi Falana (SAN) read the provision as meaning “25 states or 24 states plus the FCT”. The Constitution itself says in Section 2(2) that “Nigeria shall be a Federation consisting of States and a Federal Capital Territory.” In 2023 and 1979 The question of whether 25 per cent in Abuja is a separate, compulsory test went to the Supreme Court after the 2023 election. Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, and Peter Obi of the Labour Party, LP, argued that Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, had failed it. Tinubu scored about 20 per cent in the FCT, while Obi won the territory. The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, argued that by scoring 25 per cent of the valid votes cast in 29 states, Tinubu had already met the constitutional requirement for presidential election. On Thursday, 26th October 2023, a Supreme Court panel led by Justice Inyang Okoro upheld the lower court’s ruling. The justices held that the FCT has no special status above the states. Under that ruling, 25 per cent in Abuja is not a standalone condition for victory. Section 299 of the Constitution, which treats the FCT as a state, was central to the reasoning. The arithmetic has been fought over before. In 1979, Obafemi Awolowo argued that two-thirds of the then 19 states meant 13 states, and that Shehu Shagari had reached 25 per cent in only 12. The Supreme Court settled that dispute by concluding it would be “12 two-thirds”. That meant 25 per cent in 12 states and 25 per cent of two-thirds of a 13th. When no one meets condition… What happens when nobody meets both conditions is also spelt out in Section 134. INEC must, within seven days of the result, arrange a run-off between two candidates. nigeria.title: Fani-Kayode urges South Africa to replace xenophobia with Pan-Africanism
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has called on South Africa to embrace Pan-Africanism and reject xenophobic sentiments that have fuelled attacks on Nigerians and other African nationals in the country. Fani-Kayode made the call on Saturday while speaking at the inaugural Nigerian Fair held at the Nigerian Consulate in Johannesburg. He recalled Nigeria’s contributions, alongside other African countries, to the struggle against apartheid in South Africa, stressing that the liberation movement was a collective African effort. “It wasn’t a black South African struggle. It was a struggle that every nation in Africa led primarily by the frontline states and Nigeria, and every decent civilized nation in the world supported,” he said. The high commissioner urged South Africans not to forget the sacrifices made by Nigeria and other African countries towards ending apartheid. He said Nigeria and the rest of Africa had a stake in South Africa’s development because of their contributions to the country’s liberation. Fani-Kayode described xenophobic attacks as a retrogressive sentiment, urging African countries to strengthen solidarity and cooperation. “We must understand that the world is coming together as one, and we must stand together as one,” he said. He claimed that Nigeria contributed no less than $61 billion to the anti-apartheid struggle between 1960 and 1994, adding that the country also deployed troops to frontline states in support of the campaign against the apartheid regime. He cited the introduction of the “Mandela Tax”, through which Nigerian civil servants contributed financially to the struggle, as one of the country’s solidarity measures. “Nigeria did so much. Mandela tax — we imposed a tax on our own civil servants during the course of the struggle, and that money was channelled to the ANC,” he said. He added that Nigerian schoolchildren also contributed their lunch money to support the struggle, while the country consistently advocated South Africa’s liberation at the United Nations and other international platforms. Fani-Kayode called for stronger ties between Nigeria and South Africa, urging both countries to build bridges of friendship, fraternity and mutual respect. He described perpetrators of xenophobic attacks as a minority driven by what he called Afrophobia and xenophobia. The high commissioner said Nigeria must continue to promote African unity and avoid actions that could further strain relations between the two countries. He also said Nigeria would not sever its economic ties with South Africa despite calls by some Nigerians for such a move, although he acknowledged that patience was wearing thin within the corridors of power. nigeria.title: Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Rivers and Delta actually show
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – Rivers and Delta states, neighbours in the South-South, backed different presidential candidates in the February 25, 2023 election, according to results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. Read Also: * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal * What is 25% requirement in Nigeria’s presidential election? Bola Ahmed Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, won Rivers, while Peter Obi, who ran on the Labour Party, LP, ticket, won Delta. Rivers: Tinubu ahead by 56,520 votes Tinubu polled 231,591 votes in Rivers, ahead of Obi’s 175,071. That put the APC candidate 56,520 votes clear of the runner-up. Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, came third with 88,468 votes. Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, trailed with 1,322. Delta: Obi’s commanding lead Delta produced the wider margin. Obi scored 341,866 votes, against 161,600 for Atiku, a lead of 180,266 votes. Tinubu managed 90,183 votes in Delta and finished third. Kwankwaso had 3,122. What the two results show together Taken together, the states reverse each other’s order. Tinubu won Rivers but placed third in Delta, while Obi won Delta and was runner-up in Rivers. Obi was the only candidate to finish in the top two in both states. The combined figures tell a different story from the two state winners alone. Obi polled 516,937 votes across Rivers and Delta, compared with Tinubu’s 321,774. This is a difference of 195,163 votes in Obi’s favour, even though Tinubu took the state with the higher turnout of the two. Obi’s vote in Delta alone, at 341,866, exceeded Tinubu’s combined total for both states by 20,092 votes. Atiku polled 250,068 votes across the two states, finishing third in Rivers and second in Delta. Kwankwaso placed fourth in both, with 4,444 votes combined. Tinubu’s support was uneven. He polled 231,591 votes in Rivers but only 90,183 in Delta, a drop of 141,408 votes between the two neighbouring states. nigeria.title: COP31: WMO warns El Niño could push 2027 temperatures higher
nigeria.description: The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) has warned that 2027 could become the hottest year on record as an unusually strong El Niño combines with the effects of climate change to push global temperatures higher. WMO Secretary-General, Celeste Saulo, gave the warning on Monday while presenting the organisation’s State of the Climate Update 2026 at a news conference during the ongoing COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye. Saulo said the past 12 years had been the warmest on record, with the last four years, including 2026, ranking as the hottest. She disclosed that global average temperatures between January and September 2026 were approximately 1.47 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. According to her, the developing 2026/2027 El Niño is unusually strong, with sea-surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific expected to approach four times the 0.5-degree threshold used to declare the climate phenomenon. “Indeed, this 2026/2027 El Niño is off the charts. It is different from any El Niño that we have monitored,” she said. The WMO chief explained that El Niño typically has its greatest impact on global temperatures in the following year, raising concerns that 2027 could surpass previous temperature records. She also revealed that ocean heat content had reached a record high for the 10th consecutive year, while global sea levels had risen to unprecedented levels, exposing about 900 million people living in low-lying coastal areas to increasing risks. Saulo warned that extreme heat, tropical cyclones and intense rainstorms were becoming more severe, exposing millions of people to dangerous weather conditions in 2026. She cited heatwaves across India, Pakistan, other parts of Asia and North America, as well as tens of thousands of excess deaths recorded in Europe. “The human and economic cost is unacceptably high,” she said. Saulo called on governments participating in COP31 to strengthen global climate observation systems and increase funding for early-warning mechanisms. She noted that the number of countries reporting multi-hazard early-warning systems had increased from 56 in 2015 to 136 in 2025. “We cannot afford to fly blind,” she said, emphasising the need for sustained climate monitoring to anticipate extreme weather events and protect vulnerable populations. Also speaking, the UN Climate Change Executive Secretary, Simon Stiell, described the climate crisis as a global health emergency, warning that extreme heat, pollution and climate-related disasters were placing increasing pressure on healthcare systems. nigeria.title: Full list: Messi makes FIFPRO World 11 as Ronaldo misses out
nigeria.description: Lionel Messi has been named in the 2026 FIFPRO Men’s World 11, extending his record as the most-selected player in the award’s history, while Cristiano Ronaldo failed to make the final team. Messi returns to the prestigious team for the first time since 2023, taking his record number of appearances to 18. The Spain international was also included in last year’s team. Yamal joins fellow Spanish players David Raya, Pau Cubarsi and Rodri in the 2026 selection, taking Spain’s record tally of Men’s World 11 appearances to 53. The team was unveiled following votes from 19,806 professional male footballers across 73 countries, making it one of the few major football awards decided exclusively by players. Each voter selected their three best performers in four categories: goalkeeper, defender, midfielder and forward. nigeria.title: Ethiopian Airlines, Air Peace sign interline agreement to boost connectivity
nigeria.description: By Dickson Omobola Africa’s leading aviation group, Ethiopian Airlines, and Nigeria’s leading carrier, Air Peace, have signed a bilateral interline agreement, strengthening air transport connectivity across Africa and expanding travel opportunities for passengers. The partnership enables each airline to issue tickets for eligible itineraries that include flights operated by both carriers, providing customers with a more convenient and integrated travel experience. Through this collaboration, passengers will be able to book qualifying journeys on a single ticket and enjoy through-checked baggage to their destination, where applicable. Commenting on the partnership, Ethiopian Airlines Group Mr Mesfin Tasew, said “We are delighted to partner with Air Peace, a leading carrier in Nigeria, through this strategic interline agreement. This collaboration reflects our shared commitment to enhancing connectivity, improving customer convenience, and supporting the growth of air travel across the African continent. By combining our strengths, we are creating more travel opportunities and bringing Africa closer to the world.” For his part, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Air Peace, Allen Onyema, said: “This partnership with Ethiopian Airlines represents another significant milestone in our commitment to strengthening Africa’s aviation connectivity and bringing the continent closer together. By combining Air Peace’s extensive domestic, regional network, and our growing international network with Ethiopian Airlines’ global reach, we are creating greater opportunities for seamless travel in and out of the African continent. Beyond expanding travel options, this collaboration reflects our shared vision of fostering stronger economic, commercial and cultural ties across Africa and beyond. At Air Peace, we remain committed to building strategic partnerships that enhance passenger convenience, broaden connectivity and position African aviation as a formidable force in global air transport.” Meanwhile, the streamlined process eliminates the need for separate bookings and baggage re-checks, creating a smoother and more efficient travel experience. The agreement links Air Peace’s domestic and regional network with Ethiopian Airlines’ vast international network spanning Africa, Europe, Asia, the Middle East and the Americas. As a result, travellers departing from major Nigerian and west African cities will gain seamless access to Ethiopian Airlines’ global destinations through Addis Ababa, while international passengers arriving on Ethiopian Airlines flights will benefit from expanded onward travel options across Nigeria and west africa through Air Peace’s domestic network. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine North Korea Is Minting Its Own Meme Coins to Launder Binance Hack Loot North Korean launderers are creating their own worthless meme coins and pushing stolen Binance funds through them so the coins never move directly from one wallet to another, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said Monday. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the operators minted at least six new tokens on the NEAR blockchain — named FUK, OLCCL, MEILI, MMLI, DABI and SINU — paired each with NEAR in its own liquidity pool, then bought the tokens with stolen NEAR and sold them back out through a second set of wallets. About 117,000 NEAR, or roughly $430,000, passed through the six tokens, Elliptic wrote . The trail sits inside the broader laundering of the Oct. 29 Binance theft, which the exchange has put at $6.34 billion and which the FBI has attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Elliptic’s wider update now puts roughly 3,000 BTC — about $225 million — in new bitcoin addresses converted from other stolen assets, while about 11.8 million NEAR, or $43.7 million, from the theft has still not moved. “Most people think of meme tokens as joke coins whose prices rise and fall on hype,” Elliptic co-founder and chief scientist Dr. Tom Robinson wrote. “North Korea’s launderers have found a different use for them.” How the homemade token trick works The technique is a four-step hop. The North Korea launderers create a token with a public launch tool, open a liquidity pool pairing it with a real asset such as NEAR or a stablecoin, buy the new token with stolen funds from one set of wallets, then sell it back into the same pool from a second set of wallets that collect the real asset. At no point do the stolen funds transfer directly from a buying wallet to a collecting wallet, because the pool sits in between. To a casual observer, the collecting wallets look like ordinary traders who sold a token at a profit. Each of the six NEAR tokens cost about 25 NEAR, or around $90, to create. Each was traded heavily within hours using stolen NEAR and then abandoned. None has traded since Nov. 8, and that afternoon the creators of four of them withdrew what liquidity was left. Five of the six token creators were funded by a wallet that had just sold an earlier token, between two and 13 minutes before the next launch, so the tokens form a chain. Elliptic first reported the same approach in the laundering of the February 2025 Bybit theft, also attributed to North Korean group TraderTraitor, when a worthless Tron token helped move at least $24 million. In the Binance case the firm has also seen the technique on Tron and a close variant on Solana that used existing thinly traded tokens rather than homemade ones. A slowing tactic, not a disappearing act The meme coins do not hide the funds. Every step is public on-chain. What they buy is time. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine TD Cowen Gives Stablecoin Yield Ban 10% Odds as Banks Plan Push in Democrat-Led Congress Banks will try again to stop crypto platforms from paying yield on stablecoin balances, but TD Cowen’s Washington analyst Jaret Seiberg puts only a 10% chance on Congress enacting such a ban over the next two years, he wrote in a Monday policy note shared with Bitcoin Magazine and clients. The issue is whether exchanges and other platforms can offer yield or rewards to investors who keep dollar-pegged stablecoins on their platforms. Seiberg views action as unlikely, though he sees a “narrow path” for a ban. His rationale is procedural as much as political: it may be easier to find 60 Senate votes on stablecoin yield alone than on the broader crypto market structure bill, which failed a cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15 and which he already called effectively dead for this Congress after the Democratic midterm sweep. A ban, he wrote, would benefit banks. He expects them to renew the push in the next Congress on the theory that Democratic wins open a path. Why Seiberg still sees a path That path rests on a shift in the Senate. Key crypto advocates retired or lost, while skeptics are being elevated. Sen. Elizabeth Warren is likely to chair the Banking Committee, and Sen. Sherrod Brown, a longtime critic of the industry, regained his Ohio seat after crypto-backed spending of about $64 million failed to stop him, Seiberg wrote before the votes were counted. It is not his base case. Crypto politics are “complex,” he wrote, which is why the probability starts at 10%. Some Democrats will resist treating stablecoin yield outside a broader package. Seiberg again sees no path for the Clarity Act, arguing Democrats will insist on ethics and investor-protection provisions President Trump would reject. That split, he wrote, makes Democrats unlikely to unite behind a yield-only bill. Democrats are not united on the substance either. Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, a lead Democrat on crypto policy, has backed paying rewards for using stablecoins rather than for passively holding them, a distinction that shaped the Tillis-Alsobrooks compromise text during Clarity talks. There is also a perception problem. Congress would be asked to stop voters from earning a return on stablecoin holdings even though they can earn one on savings accounts and money market funds. Seiberg questions whether Democratic leaders want a vote that could be framed as taking money from retail investors. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine BlackRock: Security Fears Are Driving Bitcoin Whales Into IBIT Large bitcoin holders are swapping coins they guard themselves for shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) at a record pace, the firm’s head of digital assets said Monday, as kidnappings and hacks push security to the top of their list. “The current moment is the highest we’ve seen at any point,” Robbie Mitchnick told Barron’s , adding that demand for the swaps “has sort of been one way — up.” Of all the reasons clients give, he said, “the single largest one is security and peace of mind.” The trades are in-kind conversions. A holder delivers bitcoin to the fund through an intermediary and receives newly created IBIT shares, without first selling the coins for cash. BlackRock relies on Galaxy Digital, Talos and Virtu to handle the transactions, and those firms set the minimum size. Barron’s put the volume BlackRock has seen at $3.6 billion, noting the real figure could be larger because the firm does not process every conversion itself. Mitchnick cited a bigger number in August, telling Bloomberg that IBIT had facilitated more than $5 billion of such swaps, up from more than $3 billion in October 2025 . In that August interview, BlackRock’s Mitchnick named the threats outright: “People see things happen in the outside world — whether it’s kidnappings, ransom, custody failures — that motivate them to make this switch for all or some of their holdings.” He told Barron’s the recent Binance hack was not news to big holders. “Most large Bitcoin holders were already acutely aware of the risk of holding on an exchange and in a hot wallet,” he said. How BlackRock’s swaps became possible The SEC voted on July 29, 2025, to let spot bitcoin and ether funds create and redeem shares in kind, ending the cash-only structure it required when the funds launched in January 2024. Access has widened since. BlackRock’s minimum started around $30 million and now hovers between $1 million and $2 million, Barron’s reported. Taxes are part of the pitch. Converting appreciated bitcoin into IBIT in kind “generally isn’t seen as a sale that would trigger capital-gains taxes,” Barron’s wrote, while Bloomberg cautioned that avoiding an immediate bill depends on the investor’s circumstances. Mitchnick also pointed to estate planning, calling it “much, much simpler” to hold the exposure “within the confines of their private bank.” Once inside, the coins sit with IBIT’s custodian, an affiliate of Coinbase Prime, in what Mitchnick called an “institutional-grade cold-storage model.” The fund held 795,921 BTC, worth about $60.4 billion, as of Nov. 6. A Binance spokesperson confirmed to CoinDesk the closure date over the weekend, saying the exchange is “progressively restricting certain services for affected users” now that the transition period under the Markets in Crypto-Assets framework has ended. “Affected accounts will be closed with effect from 31 December 2026,” the spokesperson said, calling it “a carefully managed process.” Binance said customer assets remain safe and accessible and described the move as “no sudden freeze.” Deposits are already blocked, but users can still withdraw crypto and fiat. Users in the four countries have shared the notices on X. The fees and deadlines According to emails that users shared, Binance will charge 0.025% of remaining crypto balances each month, or 10 USDC, whichever is higher, starting Nov. 29. The first charge lands within three days of that date, and a second follows after Dec. 24. Fees come out of USDC first and then other assets. Accounts holding less than the fee would lose the entire balance, the emails say. Anyone who withdraws everything before Nov. 29 pays nothing. Binance had not published those fee figures in a public announcement as of Sunday, so the details rest on the customer emails, not an official notice. The company’s spokesperson confirmed only the closure date and the restriction of services. The four countries share one trait: Binance ran locally registered businesses in each before the MiCA transition ended. Its first outreach to users there came in June, when it urged them to withdraw. A license Binance still has not won MiCA requires crypto firms to win authorization in one EU member state before serving customers across the bloc. Binance withdrew its Greek license application in June and said it would seek approval elsewhere, without naming the country. business.title: U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Regulators Drop $250 Travel Rule Plan, Crypto Language Too FinCEN and the Federal Reserve have formally withdrawn a 2020 proposal that would have cut the Bank Secrecy Act threshold for cross-border funds transfers from $3,000 to $250 and spelled out that the rules cover crypto, leaving the existing $3,000 line in place. The notice, published Monday in the Federal Register, says the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and the Fed’s Board of Governors “will not take further action” on a proposal they first issued on Oct. 27, 2020. That plan would have lowered the recordkeeping and Travel Rule thresholds to $250 for transfers that begin or end outside the United States. Those rules require banks and nonbank financial institutions to collect, retain and pass along customer information on transfers of $3,000 or more. It also would have clarified the meaning of “money” in both rules so they apply to transactions involving convertible virtual currency, along with digital assets that have legal tender status to a recipient. Why the agencies backed off Per the notcie, FinCEN and the Fed received nearly 3,000 comments on the proposal, most of them substantially similar form letters. Commenters generally opposed the lower threshold, arguing that it would burden smaller institutions and could push consumers sending remittances toward less regulated channels. Many also noted that potentially illicit transfers below $3,000 were already being flagged to FinCEN through suspicious activity reports. Several said the threshold should rise instead, citing inflation since 1995. Sentiment on the crypto language was mixed. Companies that provide crypto services and their trade groups opposed it, citing technical limits and the lack of an international messaging standard for crypto transfers, while some banks and money services businesses supported it. The agencies gave two reasons for pulling the proposal. More than five years have passed, and they said more public feedback would help before adopting anything similar. The withdrawal, they wrote, gives the public “certainty” that no final rule will be issued without another chance to comment. The second reason is the crypto industry itself. The notice says crypto markets “have continued to mature” and new legal frameworks are emerging, citing the GENIUS Act stablecoin law enacted on July 18, 2025. Any future change tied to crypto, the agencies said, should be considered in light of those developments so it is “fit for purpose.” What the withdrawal does and does not do The notice does not repeal or amend any rule. The $3,000 threshold that has applied for decades stays where it is, and so does the existing Travel Rule. What disappears is the specific path to $250 and the proposed wording that would have written crypto into the definition of money. business.title: Coinbase Wins Full Federal Trust Charter From OCC
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Wins Full Federal Trust Charter From OCC Coinbase has won a full national trust bank charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, upgrading the conditional approval it received in April and putting its institutional custody business under direct federal supervision, the exchange said Monday. The OCC approved the application for Coinbase National Trust Company last Friday, the company said in a blog post. OCC licensing records, as reported, show the chartering process was completed Nov. 6. Coinbase applied in October 2025 and received preliminary approval on April 2. In the intervening months it had to finish its organizational and operational preparations before the OCC would let the trust bank open. “This charter allows us to bring clear and consistent federal uniformity to our industry-leading custody capabilities,” Coinbase wrote, adding that it strengthens the regulatory framework under which it serves customers. The company said it has served as a custodian for more than 14 years. What the charter allows A national trust bank can hold assets for clients as a fiduciary, and Coinbase’s focus is custody for institutional customers. It is not a commercial bank. It cannot take ordinary retail deposits or make loans, and the charter does not authorize it to issue stablecoins. Staking, prime trading and financing will keep running through Coinbase affiliates, not the trust itself. Under the OCC’s April decision, the trust bank acts as an intermediary for those services and does not perform them directly. The decision also sets conditions. The trust bank must hold at least $60 million in Tier 1 capital and enough liquid assets to cover 180 days of operating expenses during its first three years. The license does not automatically connect Coinbase to Federal Reserve payment systems either. That requires a separate application under the Fed’s account access guidelines. Coinbase already runs custody through Coinbase Custody Trust Company, a limited-purpose trust regulated by the New York State Department of Financial Services. The company plans to move that business to the national entity over three years. A crowded charter queue Coinbase is the latest crypto firm to complete a federal trust charter. Ripple received final approval on Oct. 26, and Circle won final OCC approval in July, a decision that put USDC reserves on a path toward federal supervision. The OCC has been courting the sector. In August, Comptroller Jonathan V. Gould said “America and the OCC are once again open for business,” as the regulator touted its charter push. Ripple, Circle, Crypto.com and Paxos had all received conditional approval by then. Block applied for its own banking charter in September. The approval did not come without resistance. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. entertainment.title: Carex Rewards Consumers As Everybody Wins Promo Concludes With Grand Finale Live Draw
entertainment.description: Carex, one of Nigeria’s leading personal hygiene brands, has successfully concluded its nationwide Everybody Wins Promo with a transparent Grand Finale Live Draw , rewarding loyal consumers and reinforcing its commitment to delivering value beyond personal care products. As a brand trusted by millions of Nigerians for their personal hygiene and care needs, Carex remains committed to developing initiatives that deepen consumer engagement, reward loyalty, and create memorable experiences for consumers across the country. The successful completion of the Everybody Wins Promo further underscores the brand’s commitment to putting consumers at the heart of everything it does. entertainment.title: History in Morocco! How Nigeria’s Flamingos Won the World Cup
entertainment.description: The Flamingos celebrate on stage with green and white confetti as they lift the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup trophy. History was made in Rabat as the Flamingos of Nigeria conquered global football at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Under head coach Akeem Busari , the team executed an extraordinary seven-match campaign at the finals, overcoming an early setback to claim six consecutive victories and become the first African nation to lift any FIFA women’s international trophy. Midfielder Oluebube Umejiaku earned individual recognition by winning the FIFA Golden Ball as the Player of the Tournament alongside Player of the Match honors in the final. The squad also displayed exceptional attacking breadth, scoring goals through eight different players across seven matches at the finals while registering over 100 goal attempts. Oluebube Umejiaku poses with the FIFA Golden Ball and Player of the Match awards following Nigeria’s World Cup triumph. Here is the match-by-match breakdown of how Nigeria navigated the African qualifiers, powered through the World Cup group stage, defeated multi-time global champions in the knockouts, and clinched the ultimate trophy in Morocco. Nigeria’s Flamingos celebrate becoming the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Japan 2-1 in Rabat. Phase 1: The African Qualifying Journey Nigeria entered the African U-17 World Cup qualifying campaign in the second round, establishing dominance in home-and-away aggregate ties across West Africa. The Flamingos opened their qualification run with an emphatic 5–0 away victory in Guinea, led by team captain Harmony Chidi ’s first-half hat-trick alongside goals from Oluwakemi Adegbuyi and Mary Dunstan . They followed up with a 7–0 victory in the home leg in Ogun State to complete a 12–0 aggregate shutout. The Flamingos celebrate on the pitch following their matchday four fixture at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. In the final qualifying round, Nigeria established a three-goal lead in Monrovia by defeating Liberia 4–1, thanks to a brace from Harmony Chidi and goals from Shakirat Moshood and Peace Effiong . Chidi then sealed a 2–0 second-leg win back home to finish the qualifiers with 12 goals and secure Nigeria’s ticket to Morocco. Phase 2: Group B at the World Cup (Morocco) Placed in Group B alongside Poland, Puerto Rico, and defending world champions DPR Korea, Nigeria had to battle through one of the tournament’s most competitive pools. The campaign started with a tight 2–1 loss to Poland in Rabat, putting pressure on the team to perform in their remaining fixtures. The Flamingos bounced back immediately with a 2–0 shutout victory over Puerto Rico to claim their first three points. Nigeria’s Flamingos celebrate their historic 3-1 Group B victory over defending champions DPR Korea in Morocco. In their final group match, Nigeria produced one of the tournament’s biggest tactical upsets by defeating two-time defending champions DPR Korea

entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: What Selling Land Taught Me About How Nigerians Think About Money
entertainment.description: In 2021, I graduated from the University of Ibadan with a degree in Mathematics. I thought my life would be about numbers on a whiteboard. I did not know it would become about numbers in people’s bank accounts, and the fears, hopes and contradictions that sit behind them. By mid-2023, I had taken a job selling real estate. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. You can earn a lot and still not be wealthy One idea I keep returning to is that you can earn twenty million naira a year and still not be wealthy. Income is what comes in. Wealth is what stays and grows. Two people can earn the same salary and end up in completely different places ten years later, simply because one converted part of that income into assets and the other converted all of it into lifestyle. Wealthy people do not always look wealthy. Some of the most financially secure people I have met do not drive the loudest cars. And some of the people who look the richest are one bad month away from panic. entertainment.title: From “Behind The Scenes” to “Call of My Life”: 5 All-Time Highest-Grossing Nollywood Movies
entertainment.description: Toyin Abraham’s directorial comedy drama Oversabi Aunty is now streaming on Netflix and Kava. Nigerian cinema has witnessed an unprecedented commercial evolution over recent years, with local box office totals soaring past figures once considered unthinkable. From the era when a four-hundred-million-Naira milestone set the nationwide ceiling to an era defined by multi-billion-Naira theatrical runs, audiences across West Africa continue to show up in massive numbers for homegrown storytelling. Here is a look at the five highest-grossing Nollywood blockbusters in history that have continually redefined theatrical success, shattered industry records, and set historic commercial benchmarks across Nigerian cinemas. A Tribe Called Judah (2023) — Domestic Box Office: ₦1.40 Billion When this family heist drama landed in Nigerian cinemas on 15 December 2023, few anticipated just how dramatically it would reset the financial ceiling for homegrown features. Directed by Funke Akindele and Tobi Makinde for the Funke Ayotunde Akindele Network (FAAN), the story follows Jedidah Judah—played by Akindele herself—and her five sons from different fathers as they scheme to rob a luxury furniture shop to fund their mother’s life-saving medical care. Supported by a stellar lineup including Timini Egbuson , Jide Kene Achufusi , Uzee Usman , Tobi Makinde , Olumide Oworu , Nse Ikpe Etim , and Genoveva Umeh , the narrative struck a deep chord across multiplexes. By the end of its theatrical run, the project had earned over ₦1.40 Billion, making history as the very first Nollywood title to surpass the ₦1 Billion domestic milestone and cementing Funke Akindele’s status as a formidable box office power. Building rapidly on its festive debut, the feature went on to generate ₦1.88 Billion in local ticket sales. The milestone surpassed Akindele’s previous commercial record and established an extraordinary streak of back-to-back record-breaking theatrical hits. entertainment.title: How Seyi Ademeso Turned Awkwardness Into the Meshkiey Brand
entertainment.description: Some people spend years trying to avoid awkward situations. Seyi Ademeso has built a career out of creating them, in the identity of Meshkiey . The content creator has turned everyday social discomfort into a distinctive style of comedy, earning an audience that recognises him for his unconventional approach to skits. But there is more to Seyi than the character who seems willing to embarrass himself for a laugh. Beyond the camera, he is a creative strategist, entrepreneur and businessman with ambitions that stretch far beyond social media. In this exclusive, we sat down with him to talk about the journey, the person behind the persona and what he hopes to build next. Hello Meshkiey. How are you feeling today? I’m feeling good. Honestly, I’m grateful. I’m excited to have this conversation and reflect on the journey. Before Meshkiey became the person people know online, what were you like growing up? I think I’ve always been a very observant person. Even growing up, I noticed little things about people, the way they behaved, the way they spoke, the funny things people did without realising they were funny. I was also quite expressive. I wouldn’t necessarily say I was the loudest person in every room, but I definitely had a personality. I liked making people laugh, and I enjoyed doing things differently. Looking back, I think a lot of the things people now associate with Meshkiey were actually already there. The difference is that I eventually found a platform where I could turn those traits into something creative. When did you start creating, really? I started creating around 2016, and honestly, there wasn’t some grand master plan behind it. I think I just wanted to create. I had a phone, I had ideas, and I was fascinated by what people were doing online. At the time, content creation wasn’t necessarily viewed as a serious career path the way it is today. My early content was very different from what people know me for now. I was experimenting a lot, trying different formats and figuring out what felt natural to me. I didn’t have the polished understanding of branding or storytelling that I have today. I was basically learning in public. I was creating, posting, seeing what people responded to and slowly discovering my voice. entertainment.title: “When Are You Coming Home?” ValueJet Restores Daily Flights to Asaba Ahead of the Festive Season
entertainment.description: Daily Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja services resume on Friday, 20 November 2026, strengthening regional connectivity and bringing families together for the holidays. The airline will officially resume daily scheduled flights on its Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja routes starting Friday, 20 November 2026, just as year-end travel planning reaches peak momentum. It is the season of growing gift lists, overpacked suitcases, group chats buzzing with reunion itineraries, and the quiet warmth of returning to familiar streets. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. The VJD method is the only serious modern rival, and it is used in Indian domestic cricket. Earlier systems failed because they ignored wickets, most notoriously at the 1992 World Cup. What is the DLS method? The Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method is the system cricket uses to reset a target when rain or any other interruption shortens a limited-overs match. It was devised by two English statisticians, Frank Duckworth and Tony Lewis, introduced in 1997 and adopted by the ICC two years later. Its central idea is that a batting side has two resources at any moment, overs remaining and wickets in hand, and that both have to be counted. A team 120 for 0 after 25 overs is in a far stronger position than one 120 for 9 after the same 25, and any fair method has to say so. DLS assigns every combination of overs and wickets a percentage of total resources, then adjusts the target in proportion to how much each side actually had. The method was renamed in November 2014, when Australian statistician Steven Stern took over as custodian and revised the model to reflect higher modern scoring rates, particularly in T20. It exists in two forms. The Standard Edition works from a printed table and can be applied with a calculator, which is what club and lower-level cricket use. The Professional Edition runs on software and is the version used in international cricket. MORE: What is the DLS method? Duckworth–Lewis rules explained for ODIs and T20Is What are the alternatives to the DLS method? Several systems have been used or proposed; some of them are predecessors, one cricket-abandoned, and one a genuine modern rival. Average Run Rate The oldest approach, used from the early days of one-day cricket until 1991. Team 2's target was simply Team 1's run rate multiplied by the reduced number of overs, so the chasing side only had to match the rate. Its flaw was that it ignored wickets entirely. A side nine down with a healthy run rate was treated identically to one that had lost nothing, which meant the method systematically favoured the team batting second. Every over removed was an over they no longer had to survive. Australia pushed hardest for its replacement, with Allan Border among those criticising it publicly after a defeat where a West Indies target was cut in a way that lowered their required rate rather than raising it. sports.title: Man Utd yet to make decision on Carrick's future
sports.description: Michael Carrick has won 15 out of 32 games since taking over from Ruben Amorim as Manchester United's head coach in January [Getty Images] Manchester United's board is yet to make a final decision on Michael Carrick's future. The 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday means United, who are 18th in the table, have made their worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years. The draw was Carrick's third match in charge since the board decided to give the 45-year-old more time to improve the side's form after a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October. The board felt Carrick - and the players - had earned the opportunity to show that they could turn the club's fortunes around, while the heirachy were also aware that November's two-week break would offer an opportunity to reassess the situation in a calmer manner. They are determined to do exactly that, knowing the results - one win, one draw and one defeat - and performances United have delivered in the past three games offer a mixed view of Carrick's tenure. Conceding eight goals, winning only once and dropping into the relegation zone are obvious negatives. However, it is also felt fighting back from two goals down three times over the past two games showed that the players remain behind Carrick. United's heirachy explored the possibility of replacing Carrick after the loss to Bournemouth last month, with ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann considered. Carrick said after the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa that he would not step down, but chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox will be influential in the decision whether to keep the former Middlesbrough boss. United travel to arch rivals Liverpool on 22 November in their first match after the international break, with Carrick's side in 18th place in the Premier League. With just one league win so far this term, it is United's lowest position having played 10 matches since the 1986-87 campaign. Following the Anfield trip, five of United's next seven league opponents are in the bottom half of the league. This includes the four other sides currently in the bottom five, with meetings against Coventry, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland, all at Old Trafford. Whether Carrick keeps his job or not, United will continue to struggle unless they stop conceding goals with such regularity. Only Crystal Palace and Ipswich have let in more than United's 19 league goals. They have conceded 15 times in the past three matches in all competitions. Their only clean sheet this term came against Azerbaijan title winners Sabah FK in the Champions League. sports.title: Former Real Madrid manager heaps praise on Arda Guler: ‘Always in the right place, where he needs to be’
sports.description: Former Real Madrid manager heaps praise on Arda Guler: ‘Always in the right place, where he needs to be’ Real Madrid’s exceptional comeback after the international break of the season deserves more recognition, with the team currently on a run of eight consecutive victories in all competitions. A key catalyst for Real Madrid’s success in recent weeks has been the performances of Arda Guler, who appears to have established himself as a first-team regular. Guler has been the creative spark Real Madrid needed in the final third and his combination play with Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe has caused havoc in opposition defences. Jorge Valdano sings praises of Guler In light of his recent performances, Guler has received unconditional praise from former Real Madrid manager and director Jorge Valdano. Guler is on sensational form right now. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) “Guler is wonderful. He is always in the right place, where he needs to be. Playing out wide and having an extraordinary influence on Real Madrid’s game. He is playing with great confidence,” he said (h/t Defensa Central ). Valdano’s comments come on the back of Guler’s brilliant performance against Valencia, with the Turkish international chipping in with a goal and an assist in a 3-0 victory for Los Blancos . “He has extraordinary vision, decision-making and ball control,” he added. Guler could soon be rewarded for his performances, with the Real Madrid star reportedly signing a contract extension that is yet to be officiated. Valdano on Real Madrid’s form Valdano went on to talk about Real Madrid’s form and the La Liga title race, admitting that the team is looking stronger with each passing game. Valdano is confident about this Real Madrid team. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) “Madrid are becoming increasingly solid and convincing. They emerge stronger from this matchday, despite Barcelona’s victory at the Metropolitano,” Valdano said. The former Real Madrid CEO also offered his thoughts on the game against Valencia, adding that the referee’s decision to show Jose Gaya a red card for his dangerous tackle on Kylian Mbappe was the right one. “I have no doubts that Gaya’s dismissal was justified. It was a red card because he never went for the ball. He didn’t touch it either. Had he done so, the decision would have been debatable and he would have had a case in his defence,” he said. Real Madrid are heading into the international break with a three point deficit to leaders Barcelona and thanks to Atletico Madrid’s defeat, they have climbed to second place in the standings.

sports.title: Sunday Aftermath: Puka Nacua's status, Tank Dell's return, and more
sports.description: Chiefs get even more banged up but avoid “the big one.” Patrick Mahomes ’ arm was dangling by his side. Then, as he so often does, he went “LeBron mode.” It would be difficult to count the number of times I have seen LeBron James suffer what appears to be certain calamity only for the 21st century’s basketball GOAT to walk it off. The same has become true of Mahomes, who though he has missed time, never seems to land on the shelf when it counts . It counts more than ever for a Chiefs team that can’t waste another season after last year’s fiasco and subsequent “big one,” a torn ACL, for Mahomes. The big one is not back for 2026, but all the other questions remain. Namely: Who can Mahomes actually throw to? The answer for Week 10 is “not Xavier Worthy ” after the star-crossed receiver suffered what appeared to be a multi-week hamstring injury against the Jets. This is now the second or third time this season the Chiefs' offense has suffered a loss it cannot afford. Not because Worthy has been so good or productive, but because the “next man up” will somehow be even worse. The Chiefs are dipping into depth they do not have. That’s why one of the greatest players we have ever seen will remain affixed to the QB1/2 borderline for the foreseeable future — unless a trade deadline addition or two changes things. Five Week 9 Storylines Puka Nacua injures his knee and the Rams hold their breath. Sean McVay is a football genius, but his 2026 plan is pretty simple: Get the ball to Nacua as many times as humanly possible. This is a risky approach with any player, but especially one with Nacua’s injury history and pre-existing 2026 ailments. No matter, the Super Bowl favorites’ season went sideways to begin the year and the team is now mired in comeback mode. Things could get so, so much worse if Nacua’s Monday MRI turns up a multi-week issue, but multi-month at least appears to be off the table. Of course, even a few weeks on the shelf would be enough to cost many fantasy managers their playoff spots. That’s extra true since no Rams help is coming via the waiver wire. There’s really only one thing you can do: Join the Rams in waiting to exhale. Justin Herbert’s season manages to get even more miserable. Having what is probably the worst season of the decade by any established “franchise player,” Herbert now has a new bone break to deal with: Same as the old break . Yes, Herbie seems to have again fractured a bone on his non-throwing hand. He played through it in 2025, but in 2026 this team is 0-8. OC Mike McDaniel’s gig has weeks to live. Head coach Jim Harbaugh’s job might be down to months. Perhaps they will be able to convince Herbert to push through his injury, but then again, do they even want him to at this point? The new feature is a result of Uber's recent acquisition of SpotHero , integrating a network of over 13,000 facilities across more than 400 cities into the company's platform.
